en-US.description: A Windows Event Log viewer for tech support and IT professionals.
en-US.name: EventLogExpert
en-US.releaseNotes:
All changes since the last stable release (v26.8.24.986).
Highlights
- Notifications move into a status-bar notification center — notification banners used to span the top of the window and could cover the filter toolbar, so new users didn't realize the filter menu was hiding behind them (#751). Ordinary notifications now live behind a notification button on the status bar that opens a popover listing every active notification as a card with its usual actions, with a brief toast when a new one arrives and a confirmed Clear all. Only critical errors keep the full-width banner, and dialogs get their own notification button in their header. See Notification Center below.
- Date filters that stay put, plus a fix for swapped Exclude Events Before / After — the Exclude Events Before and Exclude Events After context-menu actions were swapped and now do what they say, both only ever narrow an enabled date filter, and the date filter keeps its wall-clock values when the display time zone changes (After 09:00 stays 09:00). The date editor also gained open-ended bounds, new quick ranges, clearer validation, and a visible time zone. See Date Filtering below.
- Sort and group the event table from anywhere, with clear active-state cues — columns can now be sorted and grouped from the column-header menu, the cell right-click menu, the group-header menu, and a new View → Group By picker, and the active ordering is surfaced as status-bar chips (with direction toggles and clear buttons), column-header indicators (a sort caret and a grouped-column chevron), and screen-reader announcements. The table stays coherent while a reprojection is updating or has faulted, and you can now keep grouping by a column you've hidden. See Sorting & Grouping below.
- Neutral default theme, with the blue design kept as opt-in Modern themes — the default Light / Dark / System themes now use a clean, neutral Windows Event Viewer / MMC-style palette (neutral gray chrome, black/gray body text, and theme-tuned blue bars and selection), which is lower cognitive load for long sessions over a dense grid and matches what you expect coming from Event Viewer. The app's original blue-accent design is preserved as two new opt-in themes, Modern Light and Modern Dark. See Themes below.
- Accessible tooltips on keyboard focus and hover — the app's native title tooltips were replaced with a custom tooltip that appears on keyboard focus as well as hover, renders above modal dialogs, is dismissable with Escape, and has native-feeling cursor-anchored timing. Icon-only buttons across the filter pane, log tabs, details pane, Database Tools, and more now surface a visible label, and clipped combobox options reveal their full text when you arrow to them. See Tooltips below.
- Disabled controls now explain themselves — a control that's disabled for a non-obvious reason now shows a short "why + how to enable" tooltip (for example, a Database Tools Run button names the first unmet prerequisite), exposed to screen readers as well. See Tooltips below.
- Broad accessibility pass — a sweep against a formal accessibility review fixed color-contrast throughout (every foreground/background pair clears WCAG AA in all five themes), added keyboard-only focus rings and F6 / Shift+F6 pane navigation, corrected keyboard behavior for menus and comboboxes, fixed High Contrast (forced-colors) rendering, and made toolbars, panes, and modals reflow cleanly at 200% text zoom and 320px width. See Accessibility below.
- App-wide localization and regional formatting — the entire UI now routes its text through the localization system, so EventLogExpert can follow your Windows display language (including right-to-left layout) with no in-app language setting, and display numbers, sizes, and dates now follow your regional format while identifiers and persisted values stay invariant. English is byte-for-byte unchanged; translations will light up as they're added. See Localization below.
- Dependency and security refresh — the temporary SQLite CVE-2025-6965 override was removed now that the upstream fix shipped on the stable channel, and the .NET, System.CommandLine, Fluxor, and test dependencies were refreshed; the solution reports no vulnerable packages. See Dependencies & Security below.

Features
- A notification center on the status bar — a trigger button (severity icon and active count) opens a popover of notification cards, with a toast for new arrivals and a confirmed Clear all; only critical errors keep the full-width banner — see Notification Center below.
- Dialogs get their own notification button in the dialog header, so notifications stay reachable while a modal is open — see Notification Center below.
- A single-line status bar that switches lower-priority items to compact forms or hides them in a fixed order instead of wrapping onto a second line — see Notification Center below.
- Open-ended date bounds (No limit) with a per-bound clear button, an Entire log quick range, and quick ranges from Last 15 minutes through Last 2 years — see Date Filtering below.
- Date filter values keep their wall-clock time across time zone changes, with a visible time zone in the editor and a warning for times skipped by a daylight saving gap — see Date Filtering below.
- Group By / Ungroup entries in the event table's column-header, cell right-click, and group-header menus, plus a keyboard-reachable View → Group By picker — see Sorting & Grouping below.
- Status-bar chips for the active sort and grouping, each with a direction toggle and a clear button — see Sorting & Grouping below.
- Column-header indicators — a sort caret and a grouped-column chevron that reflect the requested ordering — see Sorting & Grouping below.
- Group by a hidden column — hiding a column you're grouped by no longer clears the grouping — see Sorting & Grouping below.
- Two opt-in Modern Light and Modern Dark themes that reproduce the app's original blue-accent identity, selectable in Settings alongside the new neutral Light / Dark / System defaults — see Themes below.
- Keyboard-and-hover tooltips on icon-only buttons across the filter pane, log tabs, details pane, Database Tools, Debug Log, histogram, Statistics, and Resolution & Coverage — see Tooltips below.
- Disabled-reason tooltips that name the first unmet prerequisite on Database Tools Run buttons and other precondition-gated controls, so you can tell what to do to enable them — see Tooltips below.
- Keyboard access to clipped combobox options — arrowing to a truncated ValueSelect option now surfaces its full text, the keyboard equivalent of the hover tooltip.
- F6 / Shift+F6 pane navigation to move keyboard focus between the app's main panes.
- Database Tools file pickers remember where you were — each picker opens at its last-used directory, falling back to a role-appropriate known folder (Downloads/Documents for inputs, Documents for outputs) when there's nothing remembered, with role-specific placeholder text.
- Filter Library tabs scroll — the Saved, Favorites, and Previously-used tabs now scroll when their entries overflow the panel, so every row stays reachable.
- The app now follows your Windows display language and text direction (left-to-right / right-to-left) with no in-app setting — see Localization below.

Notification Center
- Why it changed — notification banners used to render across the top of the window and covered the filter toolbar, so new users didn't realize a filter menu was hiding behind them (#751). Ordinary notifications now live in a notification center on the status bar, and only critical errors keep the full-width banner (in the main window and inside dialogs).
- A trigger button on the status bar shows a severity icon and the active count. It's hidden when there are no notifications and appears when one arrives.
- The button opens a popover panel that lists every active notification — errors, warnings, info, database attention, and running upgrade/export progress — as cards with their existing actions. The panel closes on an outside click, Escape, or clicking the button again.
- A short toast appears above the button when a new notification arrives, and goes away on its own or as soon as you open the panel.
- Dialogs get their own notification button in the dialog header, so notifications stay reachable while a modal is open. The header collapses when a dialog has no title, no close button, and no visible notification trigger.
- Clear all appears in the panel footer when two or more notifications can be dismissed. It always asks for confirmation (with Cancel as the default button), never clears running tasks (they keep running), and dismisses as a single batch so a notification that arrives while the confirmation is open isn't swept away. Afterward, focus moves to the notification button — or, when nothing is left, to the main content (or back to the dialog when cleared from inside one).
- The status bar now stays on a single line. When space runs out, lower-priority items switch to compact forms or are hidden in a fixed order instead of wrapping onto a second line, and compact counts omit the shown count unless the active filtered view is current, avoiding stale or unfinished counts. The counts button's tooltip and screen-reader description list whatever is currently hidden.
- Accessibility — a new notification is announced once: errors assertively and everything else politely, always with the active count. While a confirmation or critical error is showing, announcements wait and the latest outstanding one is read when it closes, and only the active host (the main window or the topmost dialog) speaks, so nothing is announced twice. Each card's dismiss and cancel buttons are described by the card's title, so screen-reader users know which notification they're acting on.
